susceptibility.title: Wind erosion susceptibility (bare-soil potential)
susceptibility.note: Potential annual loss from a bare, smooth, wide, unsheltered field: E = I × C/100 (SSURGO Wind Erodibility Index × Chepil climatic factor). 40 t/ac/yr ≈ Erodibility Index 8 for a soil with T = 5.

weg.title: Soil Wind Erodibility Group (SSURGO)
weg.note: 1 = most erodible, 8 = not erodible; 3, 4 and 4L share I = 86, and 4L holds calcareous (limy) loamy soils. I = wind erodibility index (t/ac/yr, 0–310). Dominant-condition WEG of the surface layer, 800 m grid (UC Davis SoilWeb from SSURGO).

wind.title: Spring wind speed and direction (Feb–May)
wind.note: Mean 10 m wind speed for the windy season, NASA POWER (MERRA-2) 2001–2025 climatology; arrows point downwind (where soil is carried), length scaled by speed.

climate.title: Wind erosion climatic factor C
climate.note: NRCS Wind Erosion Equation climatic factor, relative to Garden City, KS = 100: the acre-weighted mean of SSURGO's climate-factor areas in each county, or in each soil survey area of a county where they differ. Where SSURGO gives a county no usable value (none, or only 0 or Michigan's 100, read as not assessed), C is estimated: Chepil's C = 34.483 v³ / PE² from NASA POWER wind, rain and temperature (2001–2025), times 1.64, the median ratio of official to formula C over the 1,518 rated counties; it runs low in the mountain West.

soil_ec.title: Salinity: EC, 0–25 cm (soil survey)
soil_ec.note: Electrical conductivity of the saturated-paste extract, thickness-weighted over 0–25 cm: the soil survey's representative values, not a test of the field. Classes from the Soil Survey Manual. UC Davis SoilWeb 800 m grid from SSURGO (Walkinshaw, O'Geen and Beaudette, Soil Properties, California Soil Resource Lab), components and map units area-weighted in each cell.

soil_sar.title: Sodicity: SAR, profile maximum (soil survey)
soil_sar.note: Sodium adsorption ratio, the highest of any horizon in the profile (often a subsoil), not the surface: soil survey representative values. SAR 13 or more is sodic (U.S. Salinity Laboratory). UC Davis SoilWeb 800 m grid from SSURGO (Walkinshaw, O'Geen and Beaudette, Soil Properties, California Soil Resource Lab), components and map units area-weighted in each cell.
